artifacts.summary: 9-phase plan for backlog reconciliation at task creation: shared audit-task-proposals.sh matcher over the open-union-closed corpus, enforcement inside state-write.sh (exit 5) with a Bash-matcher backstop hook, Component 4b in the creation standard, and per-surface skill-layer wiring.

memory_candidates.content: When planning an enforcement gate for a shared data file in this codebase, verify WHERE the file is actually written before choosing the enforcement site. A Claude Code PreToolUse hook on the Write|Edit matcher only observes writes made through the Write/Edit tools; any mutation performed by a Bash-invoked script or raw jq call is invisible to it. specs/state.json is written heterogeneously: most surfaces call scripts/state-write.sh (a Bash-invoked, mutex-guarded jq writer), and a few mutate it with raw jq. The correct enforcement site for such a file is inside the single shared writer itself, extending its existing acquire -> stage -> transform -> validate -> mv -> release pipeline (state-write.sh's --allocate-into recording assertion is the in-repo precedent: diff the pre/post-transform state and refuse with a dedicated exit code). A Bash-matcher PreToolUse hook then serves only as a narrow structural backstop against bypassing the shared writer, never as the primary gate. Generalizes: a content-scanning hook family (validate-no-task-references.sh) and a command-text guard family (guard-destructive-git.sh) are different mechanisms with different visibility, and picking the wrong family yields a registered hook that never fires.
